sentences.text:
Though the matter is listed for admission with the consent of the counsel appearing on both sides,
the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. Petitioner has sought to quash the order dated 19.06.2013 whereby the JMFC Manvi has taken cognizance of the offence under section 3(1)(ZZ)(VII), 42 (4)(A) and 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.

3. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On the basis of the information furnished by Raitha Sangharsha Hasiru Nisane, Manvi, the Tahsildar, Manvi Taluk conducted a raid on the godown of M/s Channabasaveshwar Trading Company, Potanal Village and seized 520 bags of jowar and 10 bags of sodium meta bi sulphate powder.

Based on the report submitted by the Tahsildar, SHO of Manvi Police Station registered a case against the petitioner in Crime No.180/2012 under Section 3(1)(ZZ)(VII), 42 (4)(A) and 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.
On completing the investigation, charge sheet was laid before the learned Magistrate.
The learned Magistrate by the impugned order has taken cognizance of the above offences and issued summons to the petitioner.

The contention of the petitioner is that very initiation of the criminal action against him is illegal and contrary to the provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Act.
4.
In terms of Section 41 of the said Act, powers of search, seizure and investigation are vested with the Food Safety Officer.
As per Section 42 of the said Act, the Food Safety Officer is the only competent authority to launch prosecution for the violation of the provisions of the Act.

In view of the above provisions of law, raid conducted by the Tahsildar as well as the consequent registration of the FIR and the investigation are bad in law and amount to abuse of the process of the court.

5. Learned High Court Government Pleader does not dispute the fact, that the Tahsildar has no jurisdiction to take action in the alleged violation of the provisions of Food Safety and Standard Act,
2006.

He further submits that the competent authority as per the Act has initiated the proceedings under the relevant provisions against the petitioner and has lodged the FIR which has culminated in a charge sheet and therefore the respondent State has no objection to quash the impugned proceedings.

6. In view of the aforesaid reasons the impugned order dated 19.06.2013 taking cognizance and issuance of process to the petitioner in C.C.No. 260/2013 and all consequent proceedings arising therefrom are hereby quashed.
